key_insight: Three-dimensional URANS global stability reveals that screeching jets remain organized by coupled Kelvin–Helmholtz and shock-cell modes, which can reproduce the screech feedback loop even in strongly under-expanded turbulent conditions.
engineering_relevance: This gives nozzle designers a physics-based way to predict and interpret screech, helping guide noise reduction strategies and assess how shock structure affects acoustic radiation.
method: Solved compressible URANS fixed points with the dNami solver.
Built the linearised discrete system using Tapenade automatic differentiation.
Computed 3D global stability modes in a time-stepping framework and decomposed perturbations with Helmholtz analysis.
evidence_signal: The fixed-point solutions and extracted linear modes were validated against experimental and numerical data, including comparison with experimental POD data for wavenumber content and spatial organisation.
watch_item: Results rely on URANS fixed points and linearisation, so strongly nonlinear transient effects and sensitivity to modelling assumptions may limit direct predictive accuracy.
paper_title: Three-dimensional global stability analysis of turbulent screeching jets
